siteTitle: Ku — Native compilation and async programming
siteDescription: Ku is a compiled language for native applications and concurrent services, with a focus on execution efficiency, async programming and resource control.

heroNote: Early by design. Explore, experiment, share feedback.
principle: Start small. Understand what you build.
approachDescription: Get to know Ku through its actual behavior, with the current boundaries always in view.
features: Use the Ku CLI to build a native executable. Check the supported language subset and dependencies for your target.
Express asynchronous tasks with async/await while the runtime handles execution and scheduling within the supported backend scope.
Bound service connections, active requests, waiting queues and buffers. OS limits depend on the platform and deployment.
performanceScope: Development-build measurements: Seven paired windows of a specified HTTP and CPU workload on Linux ARM64, compared with a Rust low-memory reference configuration. Figures are geometric-mean ratio point estimates.
performanceLimits: Comparison qualification and latency targets have not all passed. These observations do not establish peak throughput gains, an overall language ranking or production readiness.
practiceDescription: Import a module, build a value, and encode it as JSON. The ? operator propagates errors instead of hiding them.
